Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

further adjective and adverb

more, in addition

also furthermore, moreover, besides, any further, nothing further, in addition, in addition to, for that matter, what’s more

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.121: verbum nōn amplius addam
Hor. S. 2.6.4: nīl amplius ōrō

amplius

adverb, comparative; as a noun, “more”

more, further, any longer

“Nothing further” is nihil amplius; “further” things, as in further news, are plūra.

Other words

  • praetereā — besides, furthermore, moreover

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. praef. 4: rēs est praetereā et immēnsī operis; Cic. de Or. 1.60 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 279; Traupman 347

  • porrō — furthermore, then again (adding a point)

    adverb · also used · classical · Tac. Germ. 2.2: quis porrō … Germāniam peteret; Quint. 12.11.6: quid porrō est honestius quam docēre quod optimē sciās?; de Vaan 481, s.v. por-; Traupman 279

    First of all “onward, further on” (see “forward”); hence, in an argument, “and further”.

  • accēdit quod — furthermore, add to this that

    with the indicative; also accēdit ut with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.21; Caes. BG 3.2 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 268

  • praeter (+ accusative) — besides, in addition to

    preposition, with the accusative · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.57: ut praeter auctōritātem vīrēs quoque ad coercendum habēret

    Lewis & Short: “of that besides which there is something else in addition, besides, together with, in addition to”. It also means “except”: hoc nēminī praeter mē vidētur (Cic. Att. 1.1.2, Lewis & Short).

  • adeō — moreover, besides, too; for that matter

    also used · classical · Plaut. (Lewis & Short s.v. adeō: ibi tibi adeō lectus dabitur, a bed, too, shall be given you there); Traupman 344: for that matter, adeō

    (vōx cōmica in hōc sēnsū (Lewis & Short: “only in the comic poets”))

    In this sense adeō adds one more point (“and what’s more”); in prose it usually means “so far, to such a degree” or, placed after a word, “just, precisely”.

Examples

  • jam satis est. … verbum nōn amplius addam

    that’s enough now. I won’t add a word furtherHor. S. 1.1.120–121

  • auctius atque dī melius fēcēre. bene est. nīl amplius ōrō

    the gods have done more, and better, than I asked. It is well. I ask nothing furtherHor. S. 2.6.3–4

  • rēs est praetereā et immēnsī operis

    besides, the task is one of enormous labourLiv. praef. 4

See also further, more, else, extra.
